summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Ali Beth and Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (PhD 1953). He held posts at Deccan College, Utrecht University, and the University of Chicago between 1953 and 1964.
Specializing in linguistics and Indology, J. B. Disanayaka held posts at the University of Colombo as Professor and at SOAS University of London, both attested in 1996.

J. C. Wright studied at the University of London (MD 2007) and worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor at the University of London and as Specialist Gynaecologist at Hamlin Fistula International in 2013.

An Indologist, J. Duncan M. Derrett was educated at Emanuel School, Jesus College, Oxford (~1940–1947), and SOAS University of London (~1947–1949). He held a post at the University of London from circa 1949 to 1982.

J. F. Blakiston, an Indology and history/archaeology specialist educated at Wellington College, spent his career at the Archaeological Survey of India. He served as assistant in 1911, Superintendent in 1916, and Director-General from 1935 to 1937.

J. G. Jennings worked in Indology and Buddhist studies after earning an M.A. at the University of Oxford (~1885–1889). He served as an English teacher (1898) and Principal (1906–1913) at Muir Central College, then directed Public Instruction in Bihar and Orissa (~1917–1921).

A religious studies scholar, J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded and directed the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. H. F. Hamilton was an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1877 to 1881. In 1879, he held a post as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service.

Working in Indology and philosophy, J. J. Johnson studied at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and Durham University (M.A. 1903). He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from circa 1879 to 1912.

J. L. Shaw worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Rice University (~1968–1973) and under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington from circa 1973 to 2015.
J. M. E. McTaggart, who worked in philosophy, studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1923.

J. N. Farquhar worked in Indology and religious studies, educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Oxford, where he studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He later served as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Manchester (1927–1929).

An Indologist and linguist, J. N. Reuter studied at Helsinki, Jena, and Berlin under Berthold Delbrück, Otto Donner, and Albrecht Weber. He spent his career at the University of Helsinki, where he served as Acting Professor from 1891 to 1931.

J. Nelson Fraser worked in Indology and other fields. He served as Professor of English Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1896–1906) and as Principal of the Secondary Training College, Bombay (~1906–1918).

id: P:J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong
summary: J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Leiden University (~1905–1913) and later held academic posts there in 1922 and from 1935 to 1956.

Working in history/archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, J. P. Mallory studied at Occidental, UCLA, UC Merced, UC Irvine, Rice, and Florida State. He held posts at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011), UC Irvine, Rice, and Florida State.

J. P. Mills worked in Indology and other fields, having studied at Windlesham House School, Winchester College, and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1909–1912). He later served as Reader at SOAS University of London from 1948 to 1955.
J. Peter L. Gwynn worked in the fields of linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at St Columba's College, Trinity College, Hartford (B.A. ~1934–1938), and University College London.

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, learning from Alfred North Whitehead and Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, Cambridge, the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. S. Negi specialized in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He was engaged in research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977) and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1993–2001).
